findings.text: The boot initializer establishes kernel samepage merging service state and reports success or failure to the caller. It prepares shared checksums and defaults, ensures slab caches exist, brings up a background scanning thread, exposes control interfaces or selects a merge default when those interfaces are unavailable, and subscribes to memory hot remove notifications where supported. Failures unwind already acquired resources before returning an error.

Initialization moves from defaults to slab readiness to thread liveness to interface publication to hotplug subscription, with terminal success only after all applicable stages complete. Slab failure ends before thread creation, thread failure ends after slab cleanup, and interface failure ends after thread termination plus slab cleanup. The configuration without sysfs bypasses publication and directly enables merging.

A family of fault free copy and string measurement helpers offers kernel to kernel plus kernel to user plus user to kernel transfers with bounded string copy and length probing. Callers supply destination with source and size or count and receive a status code rather than taking a fault. A weak policy hook gates kernel source access and may be overridden by the platform.

Successful transfers report zero after restoring fault handling state, while denied kernel sources report ERANGE without attempting access and faulting accesses report EFAULT after restoring state. Zero or negative counts yield zero for bounded string helpers, overlong user strings are truncated with guaranteed termination, and short user results account for the terminator in the returned length.

Kernel transfers adapt unit width to the combined alignment of both ends when the build lacks efficient unaligned handling, otherwise they use the widest unit unconditionally. Transfer proceeds from wide to narrow units until the remainder is drained, with memory safety checks applied per unit for reads and write instrumentation for writes. Fault suppression surrounds the entire transfer and is always released.

User transfers validate the user range before suppressing faults and perform the copy with atomic primitives that never sleep. The read direction additionally requires an NMI safety check, while invalid ranges lead to EFAULT. Bounded string and length variants suppress faults around the underlying user string primitives and normalize their results with termination guarantees.

The overflow diagnostic signals a caller size violation by emitting a warning that pairs the destination capacity with the attempted count. The fragments show no return value or recovery path, so callers cannot rely on this helper for truncation or error propagation.
The behavior selector reserved for anonymous area naming is defined as negative one.
The bound on guard related retries for advisory hints is defined as three.

Advisory handling uses small carriers. The walk context exposes tlb with pageout. The interval exposes start with end. The behavior descriptor exposes mm with behavior plus tlb plus lock mode plus anon name plus range plus prev plus vma plus lock dropped. Lock choices cover no lock and address space read and address space write and area read.

Anonymous names are heap allocated with room for a terminator, reference counted, and released through the reference callback. Fetching requires a stabilised area. Replacement clears on null with release of the prior name, ignores equal names, and otherwise adopts the new name with reuse semantics while releasing the old one. A configuration without naming support rejects any non null request with EINVAL and otherwise succeeds.

Area updates elide work when flags and naming already match the request. Otherwise the requested interval is reshaped through a name path or a flags path, the behavior cursor is refreshed to the resulting area, write protection is entered, new flags are stored, huge page scanning is entered when the huge page marker is present, and naming replacement is applied for naming requests. Failures from reshaping propagate to the caller.

Range modification prefers to reuse an existing encompassing mapping when its attributes already satisfy the request. When reuse is impossible the operation reports ENOMEM if memory is exhausted, otherwise edge portions outside the requested interval are separated so the interval stands alone. The flags variant reports back retained sticky attributes when coalescing succeeds, allowing the caller to observe the effective attribute set.

Splitting is refused with ENOMEM when the address space already holds the system maximum number of mappings. Admission checking precedes any mutation, so rejected requests leave the area tree unchanged.

The split address must fall strictly inside the area, and a driver hook may veto the operation. Duplication of the area descriptor with policy plus anonymous linkage plus file reference plus driver open state can each fail with ENOMEM or driver error, as can iterator reservation. Failures unwind reservations and descriptor storage without publishing partial tree updates.
Policy duplication creates an independent policy object from the source area policy and attaches it to the destination area. Duplication failure propagates and leaves assignment unperformed.

Cloning anonymous linkage requires exclusive address space write protection on the source. Allocation of new chain objects proceeds without anonymous locking because neither tree membership nor statistics change yet, while linkage into the reverse mapping trees proceeds under exclusive anonymous protection on the active object. Non fork clones require both areas to share one address space.

Cloning is a no operation when the source has no active anonymous object. Otherwise one new chain object is attached per source chain entry, with partial attachments discarded and the destination back pointer cleared on exhaustion. Fork clones may adopt a quiescent anonymous object with at most one child and no active areas, while other operations increment the active area count.

Each chain object binds a single area to a single anonymous object and hangs on the area side list. Objects come from a dedicated cache with paired allocation and release helpers, and assignment initializes both ends of the binding before list insertion.

Detachment requires address space protection and is a no operation for never faulted areas. Removal from reverse mapping trees occurs under exclusive anonymous protection, with emptied objects left on the list and their parent child counts decremented. Active counts are decremented and the area back pointer cleared before unlocking, after which a second pass without the lock destroys emptied objects and releases their chain storage.

File backed transactions serialize mapping tree edits with mapping write protection and cache maintenance around reverse mapping changes, plus probe notifications on removal and insertion. Anonymous transactions serialize tree edits with anonymous write protection around pre removal and post insertion of reverse mapping entries. Completion publishes mapping entries before bumping counts and releases anonymous protection before mapping protection.

Area mutation follows prepare plus boundary adjustment plus complete phases. Prepare detaches old reverse mapping views and reserves new file linkage, adjustment changes start and end positions with page offsets, complete publishes new views and stores newly separated areas with attachment marking and count increment while retiring removed areas with detach marking and count decrement, including a repeated step for a second retired area in coalescing cases.

Splitting dissolves huge page and shared table state straddling the boundary and handles hugetlb separation where present. The address space is validated after publication, and iterator position is advanced forward or backward depending on whether the new descriptor represents the lower or upper half.

The locking selector lets callers declare the protection they already hold around advisory handling, distinguishing no protection from address space read plus address space write plus per area read. The behavior descriptor carries this choice alongside the target space and areas so the implementation can honor the declared protection without reacquiring it.
